title: Why Does Your Voice Sound WEIRD on Recordings? 🎙️
description:
You hit play on your own voice message and a stranger comes out. Bad news: that's you.

When you talk, you hear yourself two ways at once: through the air, and through your own head. The sound that travels through your skull and tissues comes across deeper and fuller, so the voice in your head has more body than the one in the room. A microphone only picks up the part that travels through the air, and that is the voice everyone else has always heard. Try it: plug your ears and hum. The boom you hear is the part that travels through your head. Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

The twist: in a 2013 study, 80 people rated recorded voices without knowing their own was in the mix, and they rated theirs higher than other listeners did. So maybe you don't hate your voice. You just hate knowing it's you.
